extractions.quote: Stiff-Person syndrome (SPS), is a rare and disabling disorder characterized by rigidity and painful episodic spasms that involve axial and limb musculature with continuous, involuntary motor-unit activity (CMUA) at rest in electrophysiological studies.1 SPS can be subdivided into stiff-trunk syndrome, stiff-limb syndrome (SLS), and progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity.1 The cause of this disorder is unknown; however, an autoimmune pathogenesis is suspected.1

The symptoms remained unchanged during treatment with baclofen (up to 40 mg/day, for 1 month) or diazepam (30 mg/day for 20 days). After 3 months, intravenous immunoglobulin was started and repeated for 1 year (initial dose: 0.4 g/kg/day for five consecutive days, followed by monthly doses of 0.4 g/kg administered for 1 day). During this period, the patient showed significant improvement of rigidity and gait performance with mild improvement in dysarthria (video 2: after 1 year of follow-up and video 3: after 3 years of follow-up).
